exploit_name: Broken TWAP validation allows spot-price manipulation and renders slippage checks ineffective
description: The function constructs an artificial cumulative price using the current trade price rather than reading actual Uniswap V2 cumulative price observations. The mathematical simplification results in the computed TWAP always equaling the current trade price, rendering the slippage check ineffective.
attack_scenario: Attacker flash-loans to manipulate Uniswap V2 spot price. Calls protocol function that relies on validatePrice(). Since TWAP always equals spot price, deviation check passes. Protocol executes at manipulated price.
root_cause: The function constructs an artificial cumulative price using the current trade price rather than reading actual Uniswap V2 cumulative price observations. The mathematical simplification results in the computed TWAP always equaling the current trade price, rendering the slippage check ineffective.
fix_description: Implement proper TWAP by persisting cumulative price snapshots across blocks, updating them in state-changing functions, and computing TWAPs from differences between observations.
notes: Flash-loan attackers can manipulate Uniswap V2 pool prices within a single block. The oracle passes every check because deviation is always zero, enabling protocol losses in buyback operations and V2-to-V3 liquidity migrations.
